findings.resolution: Fixed — ViewDependentSystem now enrolls TransformSensor in attach() and dispatches an updateTransform() branch each tick. Tracks targetObject's world AABB against a sensor-local box (center + size), fires isActive/enterTime/exitTime on boundary transitions, and while inside emits position_changed / orientation_changed relative to center in the sensor's local frame. ENV-04 change-gating (emit only on actual change) + ENV-07 disable-deactivates mirror ProximitySensor. 6 new tests in view_dependent_test.cpp (Enter, Exit, PositionChanged, ChangeGate, DisableFiresExit, NullTarget). Also added TransformSystem::worldTransformAny(n) + X3DExecutionContext passthrough + worldBounds routed through it — required so targetObject reachable via both a non-Transform reference AND a Transform ancestor still resolves through the Transform ancestor (the scene-graph walk-from-roots picks the wrong path). worldTransformAny reads localMatrix() live each call (mid-tick setF on translation reflects immediately, unlike the cached worldTransform which only refreshes via propagate() at tick end).

findings.note: SoundSystem pushes `enabled` (and the time lifecycle's PlaybackState) per tick. BuiltinDspBackend silences a disabled/inactive source and passes a disabled or inactive-off BiquadFilter/Gain through unchanged. MiniaudioBackend silences a disabled OscillatorSource (waveform amplitude 0) and mixes a disabled Gain to unity via its splitter bus volume; a BiquadFilter is now wrapped in a ma_splitter_node whose bus 0 feeds the filter (wet) and bus 1 bypasses it (dry), so Enabled/PlaybackState toggle the two output-bus volumes live and a disabled BiquadFilter passes its input through unchanged. Covered by sound_system_test and swap-test F6 (disabled oscillator, disabled Gain, and now a disabled BiquadFilter on both backends).
findings.summary: Both backends honor enabled and the time lifecycle for all wired nodes; a disabled BiquadFilter passes its input through on each backend.

findings.note: SoundTimeSystem reuses X3DTimeDependentSystem and is registered by attachStandardRuntime; SoundSystem gates source and processor output from isActive/isPaused. MediaTimeSystem continues to handle AudioClip and BufferAudioSource. Covered by sound_system_test and standard_runtime_test.
findings.summary: Sound sources and processing nodes now run the shared start/stop/pause/resume lifecycle and emit isActive/isPaused/elapsedTime.

findings.note: The classic Sound node's ellipsoid (minFront/maxFront/minBack/maxBack, direction, intensity, spatialize) crosses the seam as geometry via DistanceModel::Ellipsoid and both backends evaluate it (swap-test F4, sound_immersive_test), so Sound is off this finding. SoundSystem wires SpatialSound+ListenerPointSource through a Panner node; equal-power pan (BuiltinDsp) and ma_spatializer (MiniaudioBackend) agree on structural spatial invariants (ear-sign, symmetry, monotonic distance falloff over Linear/Inverse/Exponential). NOT proven: HRTF (no second reference HRTF renderer), Doppler. Those remain deferred to v2. See ADR-0026 scope-honesty section. Replacing the ellipsoid attenuation model with a simpler spherical/OpenAL-aligned model, and adding HRTF, have been recurring, long-standing priorities in X3D audio discussion — not a novel or low-priority ask — worth weighting accordingly when scheduling v2.
findings.summary: Spatialization PARTIAL — SpatialSound/ListenerPointSource equal-power pan + three DistanceModel modes proven via swap-test (ADR-0026); the §16.4.17 Sound ellipsoid now ships (ADR-0050); HRTF (SpatialSound.enableHRTF) and Doppler (dopplerEnabled) still deferred.

findings.note: AudioClip ships (ADR-0050): url fetched through the AssetResolver oracle (AssetKind::Audio, Pending retried), decoded by an injected AudioDecoder (reference WAV decoder in runtime/io/wav/), played as a Buffer node holding decoded mono PCM; duration_changed posted; not read: AudioClip.description. BufferAudioSource ships (§16.4.5) through the same Buffer node: the authored buffer MFFloat IS PCM and crosses the seam as mono — a numberOfChannels > 1 buffer is read as interleaved frames and averaged down (the WAV decoder's downmix policy); bufferDuration limits the seconds used (0 = the whole buffer); sampleRate resamples, 0 (spec: the context rate) falling back to 44100 Hz like MiniaudioBackend's clamp; gain scales output; playbackRate x detune (computedPlaybackRate) is captured at activation like AudioClip.pitch — reversed (negative) playback is not modeled; loop rides the MediaTimeSystem lifecycle (TDN-5: startTime/stopTime/pauseTime/resumeTime -> isActive/isPaused/elapsedTime), an unknowable duration (no authored sampleRate) playing until stopTime. NOT read on BufferAudioSource: loopStart/loopEnd (the Buffer node wraps the whole buffer; a loop region needs a seam extension), the X3DUrlObject url/description (audio comes from the buffer field), the length output. StreamAudioSource and MicrophoneSource remain deferred to v2. Covered by sound_immersive_test.
findings.summary: Audio source breadth PARTIAL — OscillatorSource, AudioClip and BufferAudioSource are built; StreamAudioSource and MicrophoneSource subtrees are still skipped (buildChild returns early; they need a streaming/capture contract).

findings.note: Delay (§16.4.6) ships on the built-in backend: SoundSystem builds a NodeKind::Delay node and pushes delayTime/maxDelayTime/enabled; BuiltinDspBackend applies a ring-buffer delay, delayTime clamped to [0, maxDelayTime], and enabled=false passes input through (sound_delay_test). DynamicsCompressor ships (§16.4.9): SoundSystem builds it as NodeKind::Compressor (threshold/knee/ratio/attack/release/gain/enabled pushed at build and re-read each tick) and BuiltinDspBackend implements a feed-forward compressor — a dB-domain gain computer with a soft knee and one-pole attack/release smoothing; enabled=false passes the input through (x3d_sound_dynamics). Both are BuiltinDspBackend-only: MiniaudioBackend has no comparable node types (Delay has no NodeKind there; its ma_node graph has no compressor), so they degrade to dropped connections there (the swap test does not use them). reduction is outputOnly and the AudioBackend seam has no per-node metering path (createNode/connect/setParam/render only), so it is not posted. WaveShaper (§16.4.21) also ships: SoundSystem builds a NodeKind::WaveShaper node reading curve/gain/enabled (the transfer curve crosses the seam once, like a Buffer's samples); BuiltinDspBackend maps input x in [-1,1] through the curve with linear interpolation (Web Audio semantics, index = (N-1)/2*(x+1); out-of-range input clamps to the first/last curve value; an empty curve and enabled=false pass the input through; the processing-node gain multiplies the shaped signal) — sound_waveshaper_test. oversample is NONE-semantics only: the field is not carried across the seam, so 2x/4x is ignored (deferred). WaveShaper.curve is defined by ISO/IEC 19775-1 §16.4.21 but absent from the vendored X3D 4.0 UOM; it is supplied by the cited FIELD_ADDITIONS overlay (src/x3d_cpp_gen/conformance/errata.py, tracked in UOM-SND-1), not by editing the vendored data. WaveShaper is BuiltinDspBackend-only (MiniaudioBackend has no WaveShaper kind). Analyser/Convolver remain deferred; each is a clean AudioBackend extension point (add a NodeKind + DSP in the backend .cpp). No new seam needed.
findings.summary: Sound-processing breadth — Gain, BiquadFilter, Delay, DynamicsCompressor and WaveShaper are built; Analyser/Convolver subtrees are skipped.

findings.note: The AudioBackend now has renderStereo() proven via the swap-test (both backends render stereo output for Panner nodes). The stereo path is the seam prerequisite for multi-channel; the ChannelMerger/Selector/Splitter nodes and channel-aware routing still require dedicated NodeKinds and a channel-count-aware buffer contract. Deferred. Multi-channel routing has moved beyond a speculative extension: it was an actively-proposed X3D4 spec feature with competing routing-node proposals, and at least one working prototype implementation has demonstrated SFInt32 routing on both source and destination sides plus connect/disconnect handling — concrete precedent for the buffer-contract shape this seam will eventually need.
findings.summary: Channels + multi-channel PARTIALLY UNBLOCKED — stereo render path (renderStereo) landed (ADR-0026); ChannelMerger/Selector/Splitter still not built; channelCount/channelCountMode/channelInterpretation still ignored.

findings.note: Wired: the seam carries Waveform::Custom + optionsReal/optionsImag harmonic terms (cross once at createNode, like Buffer PCM, ADR-0050 precedent); BuiltinDspBackend sums harmonics k=1..N-1 (index 0 = DC, ignored) normalized to peak absolute value 1 (Web Audio default; X3D 4.0's PeriodicWave has no disableNormalization toggle); SoundSystem::setPeriodicWave(osc, wave) registers a PeriodicWave node before attach — standard types map onto the Waveform enum, CUSTOM with no terms falls back to sine. Ignored: the authored OscillatorSource.periodicWave field. The generated bindings model X3D 4.0, where OscillatorSource has no periodicWave field (added in 4.1); PeriodicWave itself exists in 4.0 (type/optionsReal/optionsImag). A parsed <PeriodicWave containerField='periodicWave'/> child parks in the parser's IS fallback slot and findField(osc, 'periodicWave') is null — pinned by x3d_sound_periodicwave (parse tier). Becomes readable when the bindings move to 4.1; until then the embedder registers the wave. MiniaudioBackend's ma_waveform has no custom-table type, so registered waves play as sine there.
findings.summary: periodicWave stays unread from parsed scenes (the 4.0 bindings predate the 4.1 field) — a registered PeriodicWave is realized on BuiltinDspBackend; MiniaudioBackend falls back to sine.

findings.note: Compared field-by-field against the ISO/IEC 19775-1 v4.0 sound.html field tables (2026-09-29; a quick parser that could not read Analyser, AudioClip, BufferAudioSource, OscillatorSource or SpatialSound, so those five are UNCHECKED). WaveShaper.curve (MFFloat inputOutput) is defined by the standard (16.4.21) but absent from the UOM; it is added by the cited FIELD_ADDITIONS overlay in src/x3d_cpp_gen/conformance/errata.py (in-memory, guarded, self-disabling; the vendored XML and committed manifests are untouched) and is what gives the generated WaveShaper getCurve/setCurve. Still open and not yet judged (direction unknown: the ISO text or the UOM may be the erroneous side): Sound has `children` in the standard and `spatialize` in the UOM only; StreamAudioSource lacks `channelCount`; Delay and StreamAudioDestination carry UOM-only `tailTime` / `isActive`; streamIdentifier is MFString in the standard but SFString in the UOM (StreamAudioSource, StreamAudioDestination); ChannelSplitter.children is SFNode in the standard but MFNode in the UOM; ListenerPointSource.gain is SFInt32 in the standard (almost certainly an editorial typo) but SFFloat in the UOM. Next: finish the comparison for the five unchecked nodes and the other components, then add each proven omission to FIELD_ADDITIONS with a citation and report it to Web3D.
findings.summary: The vendored X3D 4.0 UOM disagrees with the published ISO/IEC 19775-1 Sound field tables on several nodes; only WaveShaper.curve is corrected so far.

findings.note: Mapping rule: one RigidBodyCollection owns one Jolt PhysicsSystem, so the collection's world-wide sleep thresholds apply to the whole world, and its autoDisable gates it; the per-body toggle is RigidBody.autoDisable (Jolt has no per-body threshold setter). The §37 default autoDisable=FALSE therefore leaves every enrolled body permanently awake (Jolt mAllowSleeping=false AND per-body allow-sleeping=false) — the §37-correct reading of 'autoDisable toggles operation of disable*' (Jolt previously slept bodies with its own defaults). Default-numeric preservation: a zero disableTime/disableLinearSpeed leaves Jolt's own 0.5 s / 0.03 m/s untouched. The sleeping state is now observable to the runtime via PhysicsBackend::isBodyActive (exposed as PhysicsSystem::isBodyActive); NO new output events were added (the seam has no enabled/isEnabled output hook). autoDamp + linear/angularDampingFactor remain honored (force = -factor·velocity, §37.4.10).
findings.summary: Sleeping/auto-disable fields are now honored as far as Jolt allows. RigidBody.autoDisable -> per-body Jolt allow-sleeping; RigidBodyCollection.autoDisable -> world PhysicsSettings.mAllowSleeping; collection disableTime -> mTimeBeforeSleep; collection disableLinearSpeed -> mPointVelocitySleepThreshold. Still ignored: disableAngularSpeed (Jolt has no separate angular sleep threshold) and the per-body RigidBody.disableTime/disableLinearSpeed (Jolt's thresholds are world-wide).

findings.note: Jolt's hinge angle is the NEGATIVE of the body's rotation about the axis, so the authored limits are negated before being handed to Jolt ([lo,hi] -> [-hi,-lo]); a TDD asymmetric-limit test caught a latent sign bug that symmetric ranges (the default -pi..pi and the locked 0,0) had hidden. A zero-width (locked) range is widened by a 1e-4 gap (Jolt asserts on min==max). Out-of-domain input (initial pose outside the limits, |angle|>pi) is malformed per §37 and clamped + warned. stopBounce / stopErrorCorrection (limit softness/overshoot) remain deferred under CONF-RBP-SOLVER.
findings.summary: SingleAxisHingeJoint minAngle/maxAngle are honored with the correct sign. §37 limits are measured from the initial pose (valid range minAngle<=0<=maxAngle, <=pi each way) — exactly Jolt's hinge convention. Spec-valid ranges, including asymmetric ones, are honored; out-of-domain/malformed limits are clamped to the valid domain + warned.

Verified by the quadcopter sim (authored inertia governs roll, differs from shape-derived) + a COM-orbit test. findings.summary: inertia (explicit tensor) + centerOfMass are now HONORED (Jolt MassAndInertiaProvided + OffsetCenterOfMassShape; non-default detection). Remaining: massDensityModel, finiteRotationAxis/useFiniteRotation.

findings.note: Seam: PhysicsBackend::setSolverSettings(SolverSettings) (appended after the existing methods) + JoltBackend override reading GetPhysicsSettings/SetPhysicsSettings. PhysicsSystem::attach sends a field ONLY when it differs from RigidBodyCollection::getDefault*(  ), so at the §37 defaults every field is a sentinel and Jolt's own settings are left untouched. Honest mappings only: iterations->mNumVelocitySteps (Jolt default 10 == §37 default 10); errorCorrection->mBaumgarte (both are the [0,1] fraction of position error corrected per update); contactSurfaceThickness->mPenetrationSlop (both are the allowed post-contact interpenetration, m); maxCorrectionSpeed->mMaxPenetrationDistance (closest real cap on position-error correction — caveat: Jolt's value is a per-iteration DISTANCE (m), §37's is a SPEED (m/s)). NOT mapped (no honest equivalent): constantForceMix (Jolt has no constant-force-mix/softness knob); preferAccuracy (a performance hint, no boolean accuracy dial); Jolt's mSpeculativeContactDistance is a pre-contact speculative-detection radius, NOT post-contact interpenetration, so contactSurfaceThickness does not set it; mNumPositionSteps is left at Jolt's default (the §37 iterations field maps to the velocity solver only, so mapping it to the position solver too would change spec-default behavior). The Jolt mapping compiles and the Jolt/physics-system suites pass against real Jolt v5.5.0 with the solver settings applied (host build, -DX3D_CPP_BUILD_PHYSICS=ON), but no test reads Jolt's PhysicsSettings back to assert the applied values: the seam hand-off is asserted by runtime/physics/tests/physics_solver_settings_test.cpp (engine-agnostic recording fake).
findings.summary: RigidBodyCollection solver tuning is now WIRED for iterations -> Jolt velocity-solver steps, errorCorrection -> Baumgarte, contactSurfaceThickness -> penetration slop, maxCorrectionSpeed -> max penetration distance (each applied only when authored off the §37 default, so spec-default behavior is unchanged). constantForceMix and preferAccuracy remain IGNORED (no honest Jolt equivalent); autoDisable and the sleep thresholds are wired separately (CONF-RBP-DAMP).

findings.note: Swept + swung DONE (2026-07): both are recognized and tessellate into the shared patch-surface mesh form (Triangles, per-vertex normals, unit-square texcoords) via NurbsEval.hpp helpers — tessellateCurve2D (an X3DNurbsControlCurveNode lifted to the shared evaluator), sweptSurfaceGrid (cross-section carried in the Frenet-ish frame of the trajectory tangent: a circle swept along a straight line is a cylinder) and swungSurfaceGrid (the classic swung S(u,v)=(px·tx, px·ty, py): a line profile swung around a circle is a surface of revolution). They honor solid/ccw/tessellation like the patch surface, read the profile/cross-section via the control-curve fields (order/knot/weight/closed; ContourPolyline2D forced piecewise-linear order 2), reuse s.weightMode (NRB-4), and gain conservative GeometryBounds arms (trajectory control hull inflated by the cross-section radius; swung by |px|·|t|, z from the profile height). NurbsTrimmedSurface NOT DONE: it needs 2D contour-loop point-in-region clipping + polygon triangulation in the (u,v) domain, and the codebase has no such helper (MeshBuilder's only triangulators are lattice/strip/fan grid emitters). findings.note: Resolved by option (b): runtime/extract/NurbsEval.hpp gained a NurbsWeightMode { Premultiplied, Euclidean } on CurveDef/SurfaceDef, threaded through evalSurface/tessellateCurve, and surfaced as MeshBuildOptions::nurbsWeightMode. The DEFAULT is Premultiplied — controlPoint is used verbatim as the homogeneous xyz — because the entire shipping X3D ecosystem requires it: primary-source list evidence (x3d-public 2020-05, 'Nurbs control points, preweighted or not?') has Andreas Plesch ('all freeWrl, view3dscene and InstantPlayer expect premultiplied control points') and Michalis Kamburelis ('all X3D browsers require points to be premultiplied by the given weight'), the convention was set by the blaxxun/bitmanagement browser ~20 years ago, White Dune stores premultiplied handles, and X3DOM deliberately switched to it (Plesch, 2020-05-28); the X3D 4.0 keep-compat decision preserved it. The literal textbook/spec-formula reading (§27, multiply weight*controlPoint inside the evaluator) remains available via NurbsWeightMode::Euclidean. X3D §27 is genuinely silent on the convention, so both are spec-permitted; the default is chosen for interop faithfulness. weight==1 content (the common case + every existing golden, incl. the unit-weight Bezier teapot) is bit-identical under both modes — verified by nurbs_curve_unit_weights_mode_agnostic. Coverage: nurbs_curve_exact_unit_circle (Euclidean corners) + nurbs_curve_premultiplied_unit_circle (premultiplied corners, default mode) both trace the exact unit circle. NRB-3's deferred trimmed/swept/swung surfaces should reuse s.weightMode when they land.
findings.summary: NURBS controlPoint weight convention now defaults to premultiplied (matching the whole shipping ecosystem), with an opt-in Euclidean/textbook mode.

findings.note: RESOLVED as erratum — field name in code is correct. CONFIRMED against the published ISO/IEC 19775-1:2023 normative text (web3d IS HTML; ISO PDF is paywalled, the IS HTML is the authoritative free form): TextureProjectorParallel §42.4.2 genuinely declares 'SFFloat [in,out] shadowsIntensity 1 [0,1]' (trailing s) in both the node grammar and the field summary — so it is in the actual standard, not a mirror artifact. Web3d's own UOM normalizes to shadowIntensity; the generator emits the correct name. NO rename. Tolerant-alias follow-up split out as TPJ-2. (sweep 2026-06-25; PDF/published-spec verified 2026-06-25)

findings.note: X3D SFTime is normatively seconds since the Unix epoch (8.2.1), so a strict reading makes startTime=0 mean 1970. The SDK never reads a wall clock; every time-dependent system reads only the `now` passed to X3DExecutionContext::tick(now), so the embedder picks the origin. Both bundled renderers feed app-relative time (OpenGL PoC: glfwGetTime(); cpuraster --animate: frame/fps), starting ~0 at load — so startTime=0 behaves as "at load", matching Castle Game Engine's NavigationInfo.timeOriginAtLoad extension by default (https://castle-engine.io/x3d_time_origin_considered_uncomfortable). A consumer needing literal spec semantics feeds epoch `now`. CONSEQUENCE / nuance: a file authoring an absolute startTime phases differently under app-relative vs epoch feeding (for startTime<=now loops this only shifts phase, not whether they animate). This is a deliberate contract, documented in docs/wiki/subsystems/system-time.md ("Time origin"). No code change — recorded so the matrix does not later flag it as an unhandled epoch gap.
findings.summary: By design: the time origin is the consumer's choice (the `now` fed to tick()), not baked into the SDK. App-relative feeding yields Castle's timeOriginAtLoad behaviour; strict epoch feeding yields literal SFTime semantics.
